items.html: Calling me
That shaky whisper overcome by heavier breath
Weight in shakes and tightened chest
In my open ear, my ear almost moving from a sound not heard
That night screams
It's not safe here
Drunk on bridling poisons both caustic and bitter
Tortured with stirnament
Cornered into a fallscape retreating itself
Pulled out from the inside of corner
Curse waits for me there, saying to me,
“I need something made of you.”
Invisible warnings written on everything yet never heard
Now pulled into a blackened heat, fed ignorance
In a dead home whose walls are like an unmovable curtain
The draper hides something behind this stubborn myth
Follow me tonight, listen to me.
It's calling.
Under a dark crescent.
I waited so long; if you could see where I've been. What is the cost?
Pour me visions of Epinoia, inhale.
Waiting for clarity.
Shake dice below the lapping flames of my hunger.
Intentions
Nine of her parts
Seven doors
Sixteen and chained to a leash
Pray for an end to this
Eighteen holes
Stolen five of her parts
Thirteenth Age
Scattering the parts
Reach inside that needy nous
Reaching, reaching
Burn those needy words
Before you write, I have found something; listen
Are you listening?
She stokes the flames
Two more substances, spill wet ink
Presence begs breakdown
Bark rolls into a pit-nous
Two split convergence
Twenty-eight rolls the dice
I'll be there waiting
kōaḥ
Movements from the outsides heard with insights within sights; it hurts.
Motions; feeling, seeing, suture this divergence.
Whisper the restless air down
Slide that skin into a fall
Feeling sin, let me in
Follow me tonight, where Venus begins again
Hide with me.
8 of your grounds and 9 of your warmth
They buried her eyes, hands, feet, and hips
They used to have light in them
Now rooted in their eternal hatred, slaves to their servitudes
Deformed Sons and Daughters

18 pairs of Earth Element’s corruption, of ignorance. Condolences founded on hatred, pleas of mercy shadows. “Pour it out, pour it out, listen to me, pour it out; waiting to take hold. Spill that formless spills, pouring deep within, pouring into molds, my planted trees.” Emanating inside me, out of me, is of me.
Inside.
Visitors solitary in their sleep. Contortionist mind wrapping its ignorance, sewing flood suggestions, not the light begging to be poured. I HAD, I OWN.
Before the shore, before the shore.
I found her fingers below the silty shore, pointing North; she told me how.

“Pull your head behind your knees, into trenches of defilement; they're broken backwardway. The others here are marching in confusion, thinking of the meanwhile, but there are Doors, quiet with shameful knocks of fear, forsaken, quiet; hinting of its confinement to the outer darkness, find help.”
Unwillingly willing, unwilling will.

Opening mouths and eyes, pouring its dimness blindly, bounding hands and feet with deformity, forcing hopes still, shaking shuffling of tremoring deficiencies. “You sent yourself to this drowning blindness, sent here to breathe the dying memories.”
My corrosive breath, heavy burdens with insanity, erupting waves of perishment; fading births and fathomless limbo.

The dark limbs reached out and into me, saying from their slit palms, “Drink these bloody lamb tears, mixed with a slamming retraction of death machinery. Your sounds will be clicking from my tearing depravities, and my sixteen lies will be smothering in your truth. Hollow marionette, I will remember the toll of your lifeless clicks of dissociation.”

Blindness, choking out my feelings of purity, thrown out into the tripwire dream covers of sickened rot bondage, they cover you with the suggestion of a loving father, with the blanket's damage of blackened reflections, from broken mirror shards lodged into mimicking mimics.

Listen to the sounds of your screaming streams, filled of chaos, the sights appearing as smothering alarms of a forgotten sanctuary, an afterimage called family, forever felt but almost long forgotten. Their mercy pouring out from their pulseless death, filling their shattering whole with the disease of a million empty. My warnings dug into the ground of the elements, with faintly pulls, reminding me of their plans, their terror done to them.
It's not safe here..

Out in the outer dimness, hear my quiet pleas, my whispering knocks, desperate wailings heard in my misoderstanding, softness heard in my tortured paleness, firmness seen in my shaking, liberation felt but not made within my confinements, so I lay dead at the bottom of this shore of the abyss, on the cusp of nothingness. You still won't hear my long abandonment.

title: Ten: III; Shoreline Lectures and Sermons from the Snake

items.html: Bouts of restless astonishment calling inside, no understanding, illuminate me; I am lost.
I see the waves of the light, how it has faded, its shoreline into nothingness, where the darkness overtakes the light.
You have come a long way,
from its pureness; you now stand in this,
at its shallow ends far from purity.
This light touches the abyss,
but your soul becomes colder the more it leaves home.
What is beyond this?
What would make one even further lost than I?
We can all die to our curiosity the same;
many share our stolen breath.
Some deviated from those sent, messengers.
In their folly, they went deeper into the depths of their ignorance, dimming, snuffing their own, further losing their name of the nameless one; from them pours itself, of itself.
Why do some only become darker?
In their heart, they dreamed dreams of dreams, no longer knowing what's real anymore; they seek comfort in the comforts of their prisons,
Lost in lostness; material bondage.
Their light divides further and further, becoming more comatose, more amnesiac, never knowing they are lost in the lostness; they don't know the place without memories.
How can they not leave, but I might?
Even if by the sliver of skin of soul?

They get lost in the reflections of reflections, a puppet of puppets, marionettes of marionettes, mimics of mimics, so on and so forth, so their fading becomes the fading of their fading. Understand my repetition as their own, their complexities always becoming more redundant. These are the free who chose imprisonment; even though they were handed the keys, they chose entanglement to these unfamiliar familiar, the furthest of ways.
What lies beyond here? Further beyond these horrid complexities.

You cannot see how far they have been cast, but their light is endlessly divided, their goodness always shrinking, begging for an end in moments of waking realizations. We must learn to breathe, to be aware, to seek deliverance.
What ought to be is always being, and of itself is complete light, so those who fall into the deep are not even adjusted to the depths of the ever-death.
Does the shore continue?

The shore is always stretching, always reaching further into the abyss, into the blindness of the outer darkness. It is eternally void; those lost never listen to the warnings of the messengers, prophets, diviners, those with visions and moments of clarity.
How is it so still? I am heavily burdened by this heavier emptiness; it fills me empty.
Sons and daughters of our family tree blindly spill forth their emptying seeds, growing lostness; some become deeply sick therein, and these are the demons, and of these you have known.
Some of the demons serve Demon Fathers and Mothers; some serve the pleasures; others, their pride; but there are those of hatred and blasphemy; they hate everything about the one and their being,
and they understand nothing.
These tortured ones rule the outer darkness, of which is your Devil God.
What of my Devil God?
Nine of her parts scattered, but four left.
His birthless end: it was him.

He was cast into the outer darkness, of a Mother's mistake, unwanted and deformed; he could barely even remember. What remains is merely a decaying afterimage, withering endlessly. This dying memory of his own spews forth corruption onto the material plane you have left, this being his creation. He calls himself the first and only God, a blasphemy against the nameless purity and its indescribable holiness. This Demon God has fashioned your dream, your dead home, his delusion leaving some lost forever. Of him is a boastful and envious pride birthed in delusion.
Is there no desire in them to heal?

These masters of nothing know nothing, and in their nothingness, they will forever search for meaning never told, wallowing drunk in the mud they laid, screaming delusions in their fit of lies. These Sons and Daughters create crude failures of so-called pureness, ever dividing.
These Demons have called themselves rulers and forever become slaves by blind convictions.

They breathe confusion; they have memories of memories, creating lies named truth, not knowing the truth. If they had known the truth, they would only know as I once have, as you have, as we have once before, a place called home.
The demons are seemingly many, but what of the angels?
You have angels amongst you. You are safe for now.

They will help guide you home if you trust their mercy and love, but accepting this is humbling; open yourself. Angels pour forth for the will of the unseen, but were a once-seen holy reality. Those of angels will breathe a life that breathes life. You will have visions. Your words will become invisible to hateful and ignorant kinds; you will be oriented heavenly, your freedoms many, and your wants freed.
“Don’t leave me abandoned; oblivion.”
Show me the way, and bless the one with whom I died long ago, whose voice still plays inside.

Our home was broken backward by the same heart-slamming train wreck of insanity, of something beyond the world, though it has met us by the world. We had believed in the power of epinoia, expressed through the cards and dice which brought our fate full, where the path of number sights lie without fullness. It played before the death and after, further creating a depth to nowhere; now I am freed of an anaconda’s ouroboros dream, the nothingness of a black serpent, and the innard-spewed creation of Yaldabaoth, before meeting a serpent of a side from Jupiter never ending in light. Her body lay not deeper in the ruse of this depth but is depthless; she is within me, is of me. I see past the Leviathan. We no longer need journey through the carrion passing of Kōaḥ’s passage. Free of the world, it’s illusions, and the outer darkness.
Our souls were intertwined before the foundations of the world were laid.

title: The Blindfold and her Angel Machine

items.html: Born today: Alice. Her voice is broken. Within the current of her nerve-screaming withdrawals, she hears a low, cackling analog tenor start counting backward. The sickening panorama of felt symbols and patterns grabs at Alice’s comprehension, forcing its failure into attention somewhere unclear. Her body fires every nerve by contraction against the perceived rape of what she does not know.
She believes there to be an angel machine; it counts further: “Twenty-nine, twenty-three, nineteen—”
She had always been counting down to this point, counting down from the bottomless, endless madness. Where to? Alice is certain that the end is near.
“Alice?” the angel says.

The veil is broken. An angel looks down from its porcelain-cracked white smile mask, its soft reflection catching the blue glow from ceiling sparks. Alice wonders about all the broken times. The angel’s eyes roll towards Alice’s with the sound of dry gears; his name is Antony.
In a slow, humming cackle of the angel machine, Antony struggles out, “Ten-hundred years at once.”

Alice wonders if she can exist any further through every pull of sense, the skin pace with fire from memory’s fuel. She feels a jolt of a needle into her arm’s left vein, and she has a moment where the thoughts and touch no longer scream.
Alice says to the machination that is Antony, “Will you know what the end is like? It must be near.”

Antony hangs without movement of the shafts and gears, from the wires and pumps of the wall crucifix; not even the break of eye contact in his irresponsiveness. Alice is left with the boundlessness inside her, a feeling she has died before, feeling the loss of the old world.
Alice says, “I’m all alone then...”

She stands from the stone-raised slope she lay on, takes out the tubes and needles, and begins to walk over to the corner of her blindfold. She sees the blackout of her escape as a sign of her release. Where the unreality of dreams comes true, she sees the jugged stone maiden of wires, needles, and a mask connected to the large gas tank beside it: the blindfold. The lullaby follows from the seeming terror of this confinement. It is through drowning the mind that she can quiet the noisy symbolic screams of spirit.
She mumbles quietly to herself, “I couldn’t care, as long as I am not here.”
As she approaches her freedom, the angel’s eyes flick with clicks of machine, watching with an eagle’s sight.
Antony drones in beeping murmurs that rumble out the speak of glitch, “As your gaurdiannINv —ing —ing... angel —I advise you ...—”
Antony’s system screeches in a scattering bob of high-pitched siren sounds, “DoN’t DON’T don’T don’T — ALICEE! CE —CE!”
Alice says back, “You are repeating yourself. I believe I have heard you say this before.”
Escape; it helps her keep in touch with the old world. Alice steps into neglect; it’s a release worth the parched throats of a child’s needs unmet.
Antony says again, though more clearly this time, “Alice! You must go back! You do not know just how deep you are already in!”
Alice walks away, abandoning the warning of her guardian angel. She chooses to go deeper into the machine, hoping to escape its tormenter, truth; she believes this with all her mind and heart.
Awoken, another age: a man’s hands comb through the thin hair of her scalp with love and terror. “Alice!”
The man cries loudly. The smell of something nauseating fills the air beneath the swirls of vision and vertigo. A putrid light-brown bile covers her neck and face like dirt over a dead dog.
He cries again, “You need to stop, Alice! Come back!”

The lungs must travel up, if there was ever any care. She thinks just that, how she doesn’t care. To her, it doesn’t matter, as long as she is not here. To not be someone was what she came here for, deeper into the mystery of lostness, believing in a truth never told, where dreams come true.

The lungs cannot travel any further up the current. The grave keeps her still, no longer moving. The elder spirit grows heavy with tiredness here and there, she thinks. The moment of spirit’s memory gets buried once more in another geyser of brown vomiting.
He cries once more, “PLEASE MOVE!”
Alice’s blue lips barely mouth the words to him, “Go away, Antony.”

One more moment of rest, she thinks, just one more... Just a little bit more, then maybe I can. She doesn’t need any of these memories, those she found to be cursed with light and sounds; it is all too hostile. She always tries to snooze the alarm of the Angel in her ear. She wants to slip away, down the swirling promise of wonderland, a white rabbit of a white mask company, their mask stuck with a smile; she only wants to be carried away to somewhere. Where to? She would not want to know.

The lungs can no longer climb, and it finally all goes beyond distance, with blurry dark and blackened dusk dreams. A man is left with an unblinking woman, her eyes resembling those of a doll. He stares at the death, where love got lost inside itself. He can only think that it isn’t happening to him, that it’s not possible to be left without her, what he thought to be his spiritual half, Alice.

The rabbit runs deeper into newer worlds, each fleeting itself the same, and the rhyme of responsibilities cannot confine her long enough. Is she drunk, high, insane maybe? It is all just the instinct of her spirit.

The angel sees her from the wall they hang from with patience that costs the mind, how far gone she is inside. The maiden holds only so long, until Alice finds her way out, escaping even her own escape to her quadrillionth dismay. She is sure a cursed reunion awaits after however many of these, a responsibility to see like a binding spell.

In the mind, the machine is heard running off in higher gear, screaming with confusion about where it has been until the impact about to come. Her only comfort is the escape, trying to find the old world she hopes to remember, maybe one day found in a new reality at the furthest corner of sanity, where something finally gives in. Alice believes Antony speaks the same intuition as the machine that is God in her mind, the God of this world which kills her.

The angel seeks to guard Alice from herself, maybe, though his cracked mask might bear the weight of something else, something hidden for a reason. She cannot stand this reality, so she makes a world apart from it inside herself.
Antony ratchets in his analog tenor once more, “Alice! Return! It has been—ee—far t—too long—!”

The maiden spills open with the wounds of blindness; Alice is covered in pockmarks, her face red with chemical hives. Antony thinks of how many times it has repeated; it tires him. Alice falls into the bottom of the stone. The lenses of Antony’s eyes watch her drag herself again.
Alice sneaks out a snarling temper through her gas-burned throat, “I —hate —you...”

Antony’s lenses follow Alice’s dragging crawls with clicks of eye movement, the pupil tracing within a dusty porcelain eye. The hate of this nerve wreckage seeps out of Alice through trembles and shakes against her body’s limitations.

Alice begins crawling away, crawling over the resistance of objects that is her own rebound of drugs stifling the inscape. Her senses are engulfed in a storm of twisting stomach knots and a burning sweat. Is this it? The repeating question echoes as reality becomes a horror show of funhouse mirrors to her; even the walls mock her despair. The rapid torque of a heart speeding accompanies a high-pitched ringing in the ears. The only break in her vitals that may come is in that soon-to-be brake-slamming car crash called death, of its Presto blood rhythm eccentricity she hopes will finalize unto a fatal rest.

The angel speaks in tongues by seeming exhilaration from broken tenor, made of white jutted analog noise. Antony’s noises become malevolent in Alice’s fears that flood her emotions, his harshness not of order and more of a kidnapping at that point. The smile from the soft yellow-hued reflection in the white mask, it feels haunted. The cracked mask keeps its fixed stare on her, where she feels both like a child and prey. She begins twitching into a seizing spill of urine and drool, foaming out of the mouth at the thought of the hereafter.
Alice’s last word chokes her even harder into wakefulness. She screams once more through broken vocal cords, “I CANNOT TRUST YOU!”

Alice’s identity dissolves into the pain. The synesthetic hurt erupts like ripping static jolting across the skin and muscles. She feels great hatred toward her existence beyond the dream, loathing its never-ending, strangling presence. The ringing and fever are in every sense of the body, both hot and cold. Sharp precision introduces itself and finds her electric, spasmed heart. It stabs tighter, further up, with piercing accuracy at the neck, below the back of her ears, and into her brain. The repetition of being trapped is familiar, as if she has died before. An unrelenting force won’t stop drowning Alice’s mind in all of this.
Alice stops; repeat.

The thud that hurt the ears, and then what? He was pulled from his cage and dethroned of a dog’s worth by an unseen connivance. In his wake, there were bloody spills mixed with the sting of wasps around every part of the skin, covered in cuts of sliding meets of flesh geometry. Whatever happened to the young boy, only sixteen of human? The blood spilled across the age of stone tiles, where tribunals were scattered with the frantic mind of a lunatic. His singing hives of the skin take a peek, with little eyes that seep into the surface with evading scrolls across every room’s corner. Nests and wasps hug the ceiling and walls, a long, familiar pain from earlier that night that is hard for him to remember. Tears crawl from some hives, their red sludge bulging out of the corner of eye sockets, slipping out like prisoners through lacrimal cells; as they do in the hive, it is also done in the arms.
“Thud!” Echoing muddle rings like a rippling pond. Muffles swirl like a scattering storm. “Thud!”

“How grotesque!” A mask is spread with odd curls above that of an animal’s features, strangely absurd on someone in a light brown vest and white sleeves so filthy, long unwashed in soils of brown and black.

The moment finds him inventing reasons to be not. The alarms of trauma tame the drooling mumbles that beg a please don’t, in a way that can only be not. It was not him. Neon finds him behind the eyelids, somewhere far away.
“Move! Move! You coward!” The masked man commands in a growl, then high-pitched once more to the boy, if he can remember.

Rings. They are blunt. Ricochet. Sickly with spins that turn into swinging feels, further unto the feeling from new front stops. Again, ringing, ricochet head feelings, from swings that spun and turn the darkening picture. File this under the shadows that move with swinging resemblance; it swings over the view, below a man, his moves bring shapes toward that grow once again in size, you couldn’t notice as much before—THUD!
“Why does the boy grow emptier!?” he says with a rev of grit and hate. His mask is revealed to be a grey stone rabbit shape.
“No! That hurt my ears!” The hived boy speaks with a cracking, shaky voice; unconsciously so, forgetting who he once was.

The eyes stare back into the boy; his hive eyes scream with a waking rapid eye movement. He sees the insanity-rot flashes, telling him by a hot, stomach-churning suggestion, “DO IT!” The seconds implode without hesitation; no hesitation breaks.

“AHHHHH!!!” Curdles and gurgles with the spirit’s will, breaking its vocal cord constraints like an awakened viper. Sixteen sat behind the window night, fifteen, fourteen, thirteen; his life is flashing alongside red spills from children’s eyes. Not before twelve, it never could have been without beginning. He is symbolic of hatred to something he cannot know, and some eyes can only pour blood onto their painful sights, heavily burdened with madness clarity. That childhood was meant to be mentally beaten flat out by wind inheritance, without understanding before, though sight rushes with answers unlike language.

The rabbit man stops with a rugged, broken fixture, and catatonia follows from each neo-terror shake-step ohm. Subterfuge: limbs break with a stiff thrill-pump override. Like springs against bondage, his body does not do one but both sweeping waves simultaneously; flooding waves erupt in explosions of flight or freeze, wrestling like bulls, one in red and the other in blue.

How would one know themselves to be placed in this position? How would one know how to be? There are moments of pause that weigh in between the urges, and they are empty. What of it? Where from? The hived one pushes past the feelings. His anger overtakes again.

In disguise as the abusive raven confining its rot, did they not know he was only sleeping? A vessel for magnitudal carnage; his ancient transpirance has chosen the lamb to slaughter. Pretending that the lost could be depraved alone, the garden snake was foolish to forget the constricting boa’s evil they had been sleeping upon, being no rival in hate-stature. The lashing of death rolls finds the rabbit, their prey-speed pounced by the spring fangs of ouroboros, and against the cold floor and folding walls.

He sees it. Hive jumps, seconds. Claws pinch through throat-length curtains, like wind through trees. Puncturing demonically as the hatred eyes find him cornered, a rabbit, bounded in leviathan’s choke-fingered grip. The beating snarls, the screaming apeback insanity, beating him godlessly, beating him and hissing as he thunders with concussions. Beating him corner deep, and deeper still. Finger throatshot claws meander deeper, from behind and under the throat, reaching underneath it and into his Adam’s apple, familiar to the Curse. This filth only reaches deeper.

Don’t know; the rabbit could not have. How does one do such ritualistic abuse? What drove them to do it? Not even the boy could know. The evil reflected in them brings them out further from themselves and deeper into the world. The world breeds dark corners, where humans, angels, and demons beat each other unknown and unknowingly, not understanding. The moment here finds them both in an instant flash, and then darkness overtakes the spark; violence wins. The hived boy is possessed still.

He has found his lonely corner on the ignorance of hatred pleads, begging through every belief that these locked doors were his evil, that this solitude torture-scape was their own. This was not humbling, not abuse, not traumatic; this is wrestling with Curse. Thunder, though this time from the sky, spills through the window as shadows cast distant branches. Blue flashes meet fresh blood spills. The tantrum of ignorance breaks, mumbling with old prides that still fight, then mumbles through a death-grip neck hold. The pride that fights says this is its oblivion and the hell it once ruled, but it dies like an elephant in quicksand. Claw-throat intercourse pounds every merciless nightmare into the soul, scarring it for twelve eternities.

Welcome to this outer darkness from inside the boy, where clay skin opens unto its pneumatic possession, the exhale of the one torn wing first by God. The barking of this boy’s volume also rips his own throat, pushed by an unfathomable boiling that comes from violent eternities, whose lostness denies even the daylight. We do not know life without the light, and the bridge unto the light was the boy. When the eyes opened, light entered the one who denied it. This is the now-pretend human until the light of the sun finds its way.

The father murdered by his own son. Curse and debt that infected sanity, unto an accident of a million head coin flips without tails; it was this pinball that found the sliver within a sliver for eternities straight, a cursed probability whose revenge is built upon the suffering from God’s hatred. The curse passed from generation to generation was mathematical in act; the painting of the most particular symbols by blood was stumbled into drunkly. Either the cutting of trees or sigil. It just happened that the father did not know to beat him there at that time in such a way, but he did anyway. This blindness led to the suffering.
This demon knew the suffering from God’s hatred unto themselves, having lived it forever. Endless rot, never-ending darkness of eyes and soul, the heart blackened to an outing to nowhere.

He was the alpha and omega of every omen’s haunting, haunting like a black hole’s mystery. The boy, now possessed, shakes at every limb in trembling paranoia of God’s galaxy, larger than its suffering and hatred. This vampire foams out of the mouth with a tribunal crimson glow across his muscles, shaking at every aspect of knowledge installed, downloaded with behind-the-neck whisper speeds, and by silk manic roads.

“NO!” The eyes grow further paranoid at the teenager’s cutthroat pleas; they flick more rapidly back against an accelerating knowledge beating. His thoughts are no longer like thoughts; he only sees all things in this moment, no longer just the single sense, no more. The sights found him, and from him. The seeing scars a soul that shares its clay housing from now on. The boy collapses.

On the floor, in blood. His nerves roll to a halt, off the stone and onto a ledge that wasn’t previously there. The floor gives way, and where his hands reach up, they also echo back from the place he fell from, where his past movements follow him. The sounds of something unheard make him sick; the dark familiarity causes a tingling temperature sway, the feeling both big and small in touch, far yet close. He rolls back into himself, finding only his selfless form. Darkness inside.
Where there is nothing. Gone. It followed from a speed, but from a fall. Familiar.
“Save this, your place…” Felt like a string too small between his unfounded, shaking hands, too much vertigo fuzziness in the extremities he cannot find. No memories, only knowing.
He sharply inhales as light rushes back into his eyes. He stares at the stone ceiling. Birds chirping like morning. Heartbeating.
“Yeah…” he says to himself calmly, with a little soreness in his throat.

He turns his head towards the window, where the branches sway with a green overtaken by the golden dawn. The stipes, prickling out with thorns, climb up and over the glass. He sees; it is just hard to remember, but he knows something different now. Did he die? He wonders this in the calm. Where he lay, there is a wetness on the hands beneath the shade, where the sun did not catch him before waking, and there is a loss of warmth in his limbs. He looks down and sees blood; he sees the hives still there. He believes those hives weren't there until last night.
“Why is this happening to me? What am I? Something feels true.” He thinks out loud, mumbling through a parched throat, warm from the sun.
He sees his dead father when he looks over. He can’t help but smile by accident as tears break over his bruised and bloody face; he cannot hold back the catharsis.
“What!?” He frowns, his voice trembling, as tears continue nevertheless, not minding his joy. He knows he should not be happy, but he thinks he understands why he can be.
He knows something awakened for a night, so what else does it want? After all, someone has heard him and cared for him once.

The fan is spinning. There is a soft yellow glow from the closet. The hands and walls far from. Gone. The sun is leaving. I am stuck here and not going. That same familiar floating. Angels. Wings. Towering skylines and smog between, and it latters above. Those angels with their metal below the ear and inside the neck. Watching us inside our little cubicle shelters from outside, stalking us like prey. Our monolith towers we are trapped inside of have always been risen from no ground. We lie dormant in stone cacophony filled to the brim with wires and runes. My chest squared with a cage-held heart prison.

The rain forever. I swore myself to something else before this. A snake whisper crawled legless across my hospital bed and next to the ear, where the slithering tongue promised me as antichrist. Dreadful now. Nothing more. Like a rabbit to the hole, I imagined there to be something beautiful inside, not the snake’s den; or was it? I blamed them for this purgatory.

Angels wake me, and it’s dark. Their wings stretch wide above me, and I am old to it all. I let their actions pass me by. Every time, their metal glows below the neck, below skin, beeping a familiar pattern I have forgotten. What is it made of? What is that frequency? Nevertheless, they tower above my mandolin weeping heart machine, sewing a soundful weep of give-up. Angels encompass me and put the drive behind my ear, like a slit of a lock; the key slides in, but by a sharp stab. I cannot help myself to their intentions I do not know.

What they do not know from me still yet though? A devil near. My angel devil speaks to me, unlike the others. He hides under my stone sleep. He comes in the metaphor of night and makes me forget the terror they downloaded into me. He whispers in my ear like the snake’s promise. He loves me and tells me I have a joyful spirit. He tells me stories of beautiful blue skies and marvelous cloud scrolls, where little bees I almost forgot centuries ago do still fly, but like God, I can have my own land. I wanna take my life back, and he promises me a way. He takes what the angels use and makes it his own, and I trust him. My devil parent holds me tight and warms me till I am. I can be young again, like centuries ago, but more than ever before. I am richer than all the rich I ever heard of; I am above even the angels soon.

The height of my memory is a long way up. It scares me, but devil teaches me to jump down and die, and I do. I love death. Release me, devil love. I wanna live anew. When I am God, there will be no more suffering. I wanna have us all escape the escape of escape, or whatever it takes to end this evil. I know what it is like to want it all to stop.
